Optional machine-code qualification
===================================

This adapter is independent of the Cesta compiler. Ordinary builds, readable-C
export and the core test tier require neither HOL Light nor s2n-bignum.

The first pilot qualifies checked/examples/CopySpan.cesta against an explicit
u32 prefix-copy contract using GCC and Clang. The public C signature remains
two counted span descriptors. The proof uses the corresponding x86-64 SysV
register interface and the exact linked symbol bytes.

  make qualify-hol-copy HOL_COPY_FLAGS="--s2n ../repos/s2n-bignum --hol ../repos/hol-light"

Or invoke the independent runner directly:

  python3 adapters/hol/pilot/run.py --s2n ../repos/s2n-bignum --hol ../repos/hol-light

The runner requires GCC, Clang, binutils, and an external HOL Light build with
module support. It uses HOL Light's own inline-load, compile and link commands.
S2N and HOLDIR may select the external checkouts. --out selects an empty output
directory; otherwise a new evidence directory is created under build. Previous
evidence is retained. --runtime-only performs the native controls and emits no
proof receipt.

Contract
--------

The input contains n initialized u32 words. The destination has capacity m,
with n <= m < 2^61. Both data pointers are aligned to four bytes and non-null
when their respective lengths are nonzero. The byte extents do not wrap.
The destination does not overlap the input or code, and both buffers exclude
the call's stack frame. The theorem also states the stack-pointer bound.

For all inputs satisfying these conditions, including null empty spans:

  - the first n destination words equal the initial source words;
  - the function returns to its supplied return address with the ABI stack
    adjustment and permitted register changes;
  - memory changes are confined to the destination prefix and eight bytes of
    stack workspace below the incoming stack pointer;
  - the call's architectural access trace reads only the source and its
    sixteen-byte stack region, and writes only the destination prefix and
    stack workspace.

The exact hypotheses and conclusions are printed in the proof log. The same
loop and call proof generators check the two different compiler outputs.
Offsets and instruction counts describe a proof recipe; HOL checks every
instruction transition and the loop argument. A compiler output outside the
qualified recipe fails without a proof receipt. This does not affect ordinary
Cesta compilation.

Resource interpretation
-----------------------

The runner consumes the optional cesta-span-contract/1 interface for the selected
symbol. Width, access-mode, separation, result-origin, entry-guard and target
mutations are refused. The copy recipe requires two u32 descriptors, read then
write, with the declared source-length <= destination-length entry guard.

COPY_GCC_RESOURCE_CORRECT and COPY_CLANG_RESOURCE_CORRECT replace the raw span
preconditions with an explicit interpretation of finite live allocations,
incarnation-bearing subranges and ordered active borrowed permissions. The
generic resource lemmas derive the bounds, alignment and non-aliasing needed
by the exact machine theorem. Code and stack separation remain explicit ABI
obligations. Initial source values remain tied to actual machine memory in the
theorem precondition. Allocation tables and loan lists are proof data only.

The Lean side independently admits emitted permission plans and compares the
contract emitter with its own signature interpretation. Its general ownership
model proves usable writer separation, including suspension of parent loans.
The HOL side proves the borrowed-view interpretation used by this pilot. This
is not yet a formal translation of Lean proofs into HOL or a proof of the Cesta
frontend; the correspondence between those representations is a stated boundary.

Evidence and limits
-------------------

The ELF selector validates target, function type, executable section and symbol
extent. s2n independently loads the image bytes, and its subprogram rule proves
that the selected function bytes occur in the image. The runner executes the
linked bytes, also runs instrumented generated C, and checks preservation of
the destination tail and source. A second build directory must reproduce the
same linked image.

Changed instructions, symbol extents or target metadata invalidate the recorded
artifact identity. A separate semantic mutant uses valid x86 instructions to
read the destination instead of the source: runtime comparison and a fresh HOL
proof attempt must both refuse it. The mutant is decoded before the proof
attempt; it is not rejected merely by comparing against the original byte list.

receipt.json is a reproducibility record, not a signature or certificate
authority. It names the source, C export, permission plan, compiler commands,
objects, linked images, symbol bounds, proof input, checker versions and theorem
names, plus the consumed span contract and resource-bridge theorem names.
Re-run the gate to verify the proof. --runtime-only writes runtime.json
instead, without theorem or proof-checker evidence.

This is an explicit span-contract adapter. Its proof target is the selected
machine code and its declared contract. The frontend's correspondence with
that contract and whole-program or cryptographic correctness are outside this
adapter's claims. The trace theorem concerns modeled architectural memory
accesses; it does not assert constant-time execution or speculative safety.

No upstream implementation is vendored. THIRD_PARTY.txt records the inspected
sources, revisions and licences. Proof evidence includes copies of the external
projects' root licence/notice files. Project licences are unchanged.
